5 things that will pull you out
of your dopamine addiction

a phone free first hour

keep your phone in airplane mode for the first hour of the day. your brain starts the morning on its own terms instead of in a rush of other people's demands.

cooking without a screen

cook dinner with no podcast, no video and no music. the smells, sounds and small decisions slowly teach your brain to enjoy one thing at a time again.

learning slowly

spend 5 minutes a day on a lesson that asks for attention: history, art, how the body works. slow rewards rebuild what fast hits have quietly worn down.
slides.texte_sophia:
learning slowly

i spend 5 minutes a day on a lesson that asks for real attention: history, art, the body. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and slow rewards feel good again.

slides.texte_overlay:
the ten minute rule

when you crave a quick hit, wait ten minutes first and do nothing. most cravings fade before the timer ends, and your brain learns it doesn't need every one.

boring evenings

plan one evening a week with no screens at all: a walk, a book, a long dinner. boredom feels awful for an hour, then your mind finally starts making its own fun.
